newsitem.title: USA: Foreign buying of U.S. debt up 68 pct in '96--PSA.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying of U.S. debt up 68 pct in '96--PSA.

text.p: Foreign demand for U.S. fixed-income securities in the Treasury, federal agency and corporate markets surged 68 percent in 1996 to a record $370.9 billion, PSA The Bond Market Trade Association said.
In 1995, foreigners purchased $220.7 billion of the securities, PSA said.

"The sharp increase in foreign purchases was a result of a strong U.S. economy, a stable and relatively attractive interest rate environment and continued appreciation of the U.S. dollar relative to global currencies," Andy Nybo, PSA's vice president of market statistics, said in a statement.
U.S. Treasuries drew most of the foreign investment, with foreign purchases rising to $244.2 billion in 1996 from $134.1 billion in 1995, PSA said.
Corporate debt ranked second, rising to $77.4 billion from $57.9 billion.
Foreign investment in agency debt rose to $49.3 billion from $28.7 billion.
